channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Officially Notifies UN of Withdrawal from International Criminal Court
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has officially informed the United Nations of its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC). The withdrawal will become effective on November 20, 2027, one year after the notification. Tajikistan is the fourth country to begin the formal withdrawal process since the US called for dismantling the court.

item.title: Uzbekistan Joins Protocol to Combat Illegal Aircraft Seizures
item.description: Uzbekistan is strengthening legal mechanisms for aviation security by acceding to a protocol supplementing the Convention on the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft. This move aims to enhance the security of air transport and effectively counter cross-border crimes in civil aviation. The decision follows discussions on the outcomes of the Uzbek President's state visit to Oman.

item.title: Global Nuclear Power Map Evolves: New Plants Under Construction and Market Entrants
item.description: The global nuclear power landscape is shifting, with 82 new reactors under construction worldwide. While 39 countries support tripling nuclear capacity by 2050, development varies, with some nations expanding existing facilities and others embarking on new projects. Russia's Rosatom leads in foreign construction, with projects in China, India, Turkey, Egypt, Bangladesh, Iran, Hungary, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Poland Strengthen Parliamentary and Economic Ties
item.description: Uzbekistan and Poland are enhancing their inter-parliamentary and economic cooperation. A Polish delegation visited the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis to discuss strengthening parliamentary diplomacy and expanding exchanges. Both sides emphasized activating friendship groups and exchanging experiences in lawmaking and local governance. Economic indicators show steady growth, with trade turnover reaching $397.6 million in 2025.

item.title: Economic Cooperation with Germany Expands at Tashkent Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan's economic cooperation with Germany is expanding. The V International Forum 'Honesty in Business' in Tashkent brought together experts and officials to discuss improving the business environment and protecting private sector rights. The Business Ombudsman of Uzbekistan met with German Embassy representatives to discuss expanding bilateral economic ties, investor protection, and creating a transparent business environment.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan Enhance Tourism and Cultural Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Jordan are strengthening bilateral relations, particularly in tourism and cultural exchange. Both nations, rich in history and cultural heritage along the Silk Road and with unique attractions, see tourism as a key area for growth. Diplomatic relations established in 1993 have seen significant activation in recent years, with a state visit by Jordan's King Abdullah II marking a new phase.

item.title: UN COP31 climate conference concludes without agreement on fossil fuels
item.description: The UN COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended without a final agreement, as participants failed to reach consensus on fossil fuels. The summit, the longest in UN history, extended two days past its official end date and was the first since 2009 to conclude without a general declaration. Disagreements over language regarding fossil fuels and financial aid for climate-vulnerable nations hindered progress.

item.title: Uzbekistan's President arrives in Jordan for state visit
item.description: Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife have arrived in Jordan for a state visit. They were welcomed at Queen Alia International Airport by King Abdullah II and Queen Rania. Key events include high-level talks on November 24 in Amman to discuss trade, investment, and joint projects, followed by a business forum.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Code on Administrative Court Proceedings
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber has reviewed and approved a new Code of Administrative Court Proceedings in its second reading. The document enhances judicial protection for citizens and entrepreneurs, expanding the powers of administrative courts and clarifying procedures for challenging administrative acts.

item.title: Private Enterprise Fined Over 4 Billion Soums for Illegal Pine Tree Logging in Fergana
item.description: A private enterprise in Fergana has been fined over 4 billion soums for illegally cutting down 26 Eldar pines without permission. The environmental damage was assessed at 810.48 million soums. Materials have been sent to the prosecutor's office for legal evaluation.

item.title: Tajikistan Officially Notifies UN of Withdrawal from International Criminal Court
item.description: Tajikistan has officially informed the UN of its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC). The withdrawal will take effect on November 20, 2027, one year after the notification. The country had signed the Rome Statute in 1998 and ratified it in 2000.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Double Tourism Numbers by 2030, Prioritizing Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan has set ambitious tourism goals, aiming to double foreign tourist arrivals to 20 million annually by 2030 and increase tourism's share in GDP to 7%. The strategy emphasizes service quality, improved transport links, and a doubling of 4- and 5-star hotels. New tourism products and routes are being developed to boost the sector.

item.title: Man Returning from Iran Murdered by Unidentified Gunmen in Badghis
item.description: A man who recently returned to Afghanistan from Iran was killed by unidentified gunmen in the Qadis District of Badghis Province. The incident occurred last night while he was traveling from the provincial capital. The motive and perpetrators remain unknown. Security concerns are rising in the region.

item.title: UN UNFPA Provides Psychosocial Support to Over 13,000 Afghan Women and Girls
item.description: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) has provided mental health support to over 13,000 women and girls in Afghanistan through psychosocial counseling centers. Services were offered from July to October in Badakhshan, Helmand, and Kunduz provinces, with support from the European Commission's ECHO. The centers aim to help women cope with psychological and economic challenges.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev, Trump, and Xi Expressed Support for Jensen Huang Before Nvidia Return
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, former US President Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping publicly voiced support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang prior to his reinstatement. Tokayev praised Huang's contributions at a forum in Astana, while Trump advocated for his return, citing a "learned lesson."

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister: US and Israel Failed to Achieve Goals Against Iran
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi stated that the United States and Israel exerted significant pressure on Iran over the past two years but failed to achieve their objectives. He asserted that Iran's resistance overcame these political and economic pressures, including wars and assassinations, despite the US possessing superior military capabilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Changing State Emblem and Awards Due to Alphabet Reform
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to update inscriptions on its state emblem and national awards to align with the new Uzbek alphabet. Draft documents are due by April 2027 for review by the cabinet of ministers. The changes involve replacing specific letter combinations with single letters, reflecting a broader societal shift towards the updated alphabet.

item.title: Islamic Finance Innovation and Knowledge Hub Launched in Afghanistan
item.description: A new research hub dedicated to advancing Islamic banking and finance has been inaugurated in Afghanistan. Officials highlighted its potential to strengthen the country's financial system and support the transition from conventional to Islamic banking, despite facing economic challenges.

item.title: Accountants in Kazakhstan's Aktobe Region Sentenced for Multi-Million Tenge Embezzlement
item.description: Three accountants from a lyceum in Kazakhstan's Aktobe region have been sentenced to prison for embezzling 82 million budget tenge. They allegedly created fake salary payments to employees, with the excess funds being cashed out and given to the defendants. Sentences range from seven to eight years.

item.title: Former Zhejiang Deputy Governor Sentenced to Death for Bribery
item.description: Gao Xingfu, former deputy governor of China's Zhejiang province, has been sentenced to death for accepting bribes totaling approximately $28.76 million. The court found that his actions caused significant harm to state and public interests. His execution is suspended for two years, considering his confession and cooperation with the investigation. All his personal property will be confiscated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Ban Foreigners from Surrogacy Services
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing to prohibit foreigners from using surrogacy services, allowing only local citizens for medical reasons. This move aims to combat the growing risk of child trafficking associated with international surrogacy agreements. Interdepartmental commission has drafted legislative changes, which will be open for public discussion soon.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Arrives in Jordan for State Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, accompanied by his wife, has arrived in Jordan for a state visit. Upon arrival, the distinguished guests were greeted by an honor guard. Leaders of both countries welcomed members of their official delegations and reviewed the honor guard.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Congress Hall with 1,000 Seats Under Construction in Karakol
item.description: The state enterprise 'KyrgyzStroy' is constructing a modern congress hall with a capacity of 1,000 seats in Karakol, Kyrgyzstan. The project, funded by the stabilization fund, began in May. The foundation and first-floor slab are complete, with work now progressing on the second floor's formwork.

item.title: Afghan Women Demand Justice and Accountability at Madrid Summit
item.description: Afghan women leaders, athletes, and activists urged accountability for Taliban abuses and international support for women's rights at a Madrid summit. They warned that lasting peace is impossible while women are excluded from public life and decision-making. Spain's Foreign Minister pledged continued humanitarian support and backing for investigations into abuses.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Officials illegally charged fees for passport replacement, refunds issued
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Talgar district, Almaty region, discovered illegal state fee collection from citizens exempt by law. This included parents of children with disabilities. Officials have been disciplined, and all illegally collected funds will be returned. An investigation into similar cases is underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan, US, China leaders expressed support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev praised cooperation with Nvidia, calling CEO Jensen Huang a "legendary engineer." US President Donald Trump publicly supported Huang's return as CEO, stating he would not oppose the decision. Chinese President Xi Jinping also reportedly valued Huang's talent.

item.title: Afghanistan's Exports Rise 7 Percent Despite Pakistan Trade Route Closures
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid stated that Afghanistan's exports have increased by seven percent despite the closure of trade routes through Pakistan. Alternative routes have been established for Afghan products, and trade continues with China, India, and Central Asian countries. This comes amid ongoing tensions affecting trade relations with Pakistan.

item.title: Irkeshtam Border Crossing Sees Record Cargo Throughput Exceeding 4 Million Tons
item.description: Cargo transportation through the Irkeshtam border crossing on the Chinese-Kyrgyzstan border has surpassed 4 million tons in 2026, a historic high. This increase is attributed to the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project, which facilitates the transport of construction materials and other goods. The crossing now operates 24/7.

item.title: British Swimmer Completes Strait of Hormuz Swim Amidst Regional Conflict
item.description: British long-distance swimmer and UN Ocean Advocate Lewis Pugh swam approximately 15 kilometers across the Strait of Hormuz over three days. The swim aimed to draw global attention to the environmental damage to marine ecosystems caused by the ongoing conflict. This marks the first such long-distance swim in the Strait since the conflict began in March 2026.

item.title: Dushanbe taxi drivers to no longer pay daily 100 somoni fee
item.description: Dushanbe's mayor and head of the Digital Reform Commission has decided to stop the daily 100 somoni fee for taxi drivers in the capital. The decision was made on November 23rd, but the effective date is unclear, possibly January 1, 2027. Drivers had expressed dissatisfaction with the fee, citing low profits.

item.title: Court Overturns Release of Former Zhambyl Region Governor Karim Kokrekbayev
item.description: The Almaty Regional Court has overturned a lower court's decision to release former Zhambyl region governor Karim Kokrekbayev from prison due to illness. Prosecutors had appealed the release, stating his condition did not meet the criteria for exemption from serving his sentence.

item.title: Tashkent Police Dismantle Drug Network Involving University Students
item.description: Tashkent law enforcement has busted a drug network that included university students selling synthetic drugs online and via hidden drop-off points. During the operation, police seized significant quantities of mephedrone, MDMA, and cocaine. The network allegedly operated for six months, receiving drugs from abroad.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan faces challenges with sanctions, investment, and international reputation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is liquidating 'Processing KG' following UK sanctions. The country faces risks in banking and crypto sectors, threatening foreign investment due to unpredictable procedures and lack of transparency. Additionally, Kyrgyzstan faces issues with migrant document processing in Russia and a widening pension gap between regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Clarifies 15% Electricity Prepayment for Businesses
item.description: Uzbekistan's 'Regional Electric Networks' clarified that the 15% electricity prepayment benefit applies only to 'exemplary consumers.' Companies must meet criteria like automated metering and no overdue debt. The benefit is automatically granted based on data, not requiring a separate application.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Overturns Early Release of Former Akim Karim Kokirekbaev
item.description: The Almaty Regional Court overturned a decision to release former Akim of Zhambyl region, Karim Kokirekbaev, early due to health reasons. The appellate court found gross violations of legal requirements by the first instance court. Kokirekbaev's condition does not meet the criteria for release.

item.title: Drug Courier with Half a Kilogram of Substance Arrested in Shymkent
item.description: Police in Shymkent arrested a man distributing drugs, who was acting as a courier and packer for an online drug store. Approximately 500 grams of a narcotic substance, considered a large quantity, was found. The suspect used a rented apartment for illegal activities.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Japan Foreign Ministers Outline Steps for Enhanced Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi met with Japan's Special Representative for Central Asia, Tomoaki Ishigaki, in Astana. They discussed the progress of agreements from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's December 2025 visit to Japan. Discussions also covered prospects for developing trade, economic, and investment cooperation, as well as collaboration within the "Central Asia + Japan" format. Both sides affirmed their interest in strengthening the expanded strategic partnership.

item.title: 13 Convicted Kyrgyz Citizens Transferred from Foreign Prisons to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Thirteen convicted Kyrgyz citizens have been transferred from prisons abroad to Kyrgyzstan following appeals to the president. The Prosecutor General's Office reported that positive decisions were made on 13 out of 21 received appeals, with four applicants being denied.

item.title: Ukraine Confirms Attack on Russian Ships in Libyan Waters
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian security forces attacked a Russian military ship and a cargo ship in Libyan waters. The attack, using seven naval drones, reportedly sank the Russian military vessel 'Mercury'. The Kremlin has stated the Ministry of Defense will provide further details.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Security Chief Admits Violations in Property Repatriation
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNБ), Maksat Asanaliev, has acknowledged that violations occurred during the process of returning property to state ownership as part of anti-corruption efforts. He stated that the GKNБ is taking measures to prevent similar situations in the future.
